queue.title: If a panel group was COLLAPSED on your screen rather than merely behind another tab, the new menu cannot expand it either — the library keeps that control private. This is the live hypothesis for why you could not open those tabs, and one answer from you settles whether it matters.

The colour warning we just built reaches a tool but not the window: the panel's own colour lookup has no clock to compare against, so it cannot tell whether the picture may disagree. Same answer, two surfaces, and only one of them says it.

A tool that asks the emulator to stop and waits ten seconds can be told 'it never stopped' after waiting ZERO milliseconds, with the game still running — a wrong answer, not a slow one. Real and worth fixing on its own merits; the other team turns out NOT to depend on it, so it sits behind the things you asked for tonight.

The Objects tab dumps its pool layout as a paragraph of raw JSON and pads its table with empty rows. Ship the readable half, and answer your rings question ON the panel: rings never take an object slot, so a rings count goes beside the object count with the one-sentence why. The ceiling stays stated-unknown until aeon exports it — a confident wrong number is worse than an honest gap.

The symbol file every client loads carries hundreds of build-time constants and not one is reachable from anything we serve. Read them as LINES IN THE FILE, never as symbols, and never pin how many there are — the count differs between the debug and release builds of the same game. The handful that vary per game are absent from the file entirely; that half is a toolchain change another lane has now booked.
Your command line for the debug window. Deliberately after the nav: build the shortcut before the signposted route and the route ends up designed around the shortcut.

Our contract check stopped reading the contract team's live folder today; the honest cost is that an ordinary run no longer notices them moving on. Fix is a nightly that reports drift without blocking anyone. Nothing new to build.

Video memory can be written while the game runs and the other three memory spaces cannot. Our emulator is following the written rules exactly; the rules are what look wrong. Needs raising with the contract team; gates nothing.

A weekly check that the emulator itself has not drifted, since other teams' tests run inside it and a regression there could make one of their checks pass for no reason. Existing suites only; an afternoon at most.

Five checks on how we read symbol listings now sit out, because the file they compared against lives in another project and is not version-controlled. Freezing a small excerpt as our own would give the coverage back with no outside dependency.
Nothing on the emulator's own test side checks that a negative vertical position survives being read. Correct today; a regression would pass unnoticed.

Residual from the acceptance-table hardening: the gap in how the table reads raw strings is real, but four probes could not produce a dangerous case from it. Either prove the shape or close it as theoretical.

Eight advertised-but-unserved debugger methods, all correctly waiting: three whose consumer asked us not to pre-build, two needing a part of the emulator not compiled in, one the consumer does not want, two parked as no-ops.
The wiki-emulator spike you approved, on Opus, with the report-the-wall condition.
Serves 56 methods, verified by spawning the binary. It reads the emulator's own chrome, not game pixels, so it does not end their eyeball requests. Left: never run against a real window.
